tool.name: Cyclospora PyEuk
tool.description: cluster specimens from a CDC haplotype sheet (KING-wIBS distance + label-free clustering)

param.name: sheet
param.label: Haplotype data sheet (CDC HDS wide format)
param.help: Rows are specimens, columns are haplotype names, 'X' marks presence and an empty cell absence. An ENTIRELY empty locus block means the locus was NOT CALLED; PyEuk handles that as dropout rather than as absence. Produced by the 'Cyclospora HDS sheet' tool. The first column must be named Seq_ID.

param.name: mode
param.label: Cluster threshold calibration
param.help: Label-free is the default and is what the pre-registered analysis used: PyEuk never sees an epidemiological label and picks k from the dendrogram merge-height gap knee. Supply gold-standard labels only if you genuinely have them; the result is then no longer a blind prediction.
param.option: Supervised — calibrate the threshold from gold-standard cluster labels

param.name: gold
param.label: Gold-standard cluster labels
param.help: Two columns with a header: Seq_ID and Cluster_alias. Only specimens present in both this file and the distance matrix are used to calibrate.

param.name: stringency
param.label: Stringency (%)
param.help: Percentage of within-cluster pairs that must fall at or below the calibrated threshold before a k is accepted.

param.name: robust
param.label: Robust threshold calibration
param.help: Yes: median + 3 * 1.4826 * MAD of the within-cluster distances. No: mean + 3 * standard deviation.

param.name: default_threshold
param.label: Fallback threshold
param.help: Used only if no gold-standard specimen pair overlaps the distance matrix.

param.name: min_completeness
param.label: Minimum specimen completeness
param.help: A specimen enters the distance matrix only if at least this fraction of the sheet's haplotype columns are marked 'X'. PyEuk's default is 0.10; on the 153-specimen reference sheet it keeps 144 of 153.

param.name: k_min
param.label: Minimum number of clusters to consider
param.help: Held at 2 by PyEuk to guard against collapsing everything into a single cluster.

param.name: k_max
param.label: Maximum number of clusters to consider

param.name: report_excluded
param.label: Report excluded specimens as cluster -1
param.help: Yes: specimens dropped by the completeness filter still appear in the cluster table with Assigned_cluster = -1, so no specimen disappears silently. No: they are omitted, which reproduces PyEuk's own output file exactly.

tool.help:
**Cyclospora PyEuk** — turn a CDC haplotype data sheet into a specimen distance matrix and outbreak cluster assignments.
This is stage 7-8 of the *Cyclospora cayetanensis* amplicon typing arm. It runs two PyEuk calls and nothing else:
1. `PyEukDistanceEngine.compute_revised_wibs_matrix(sheet)` — binary KING-robust weighted identity-by-state, with pairwise-complete locus dropout handling and an exact positive-semi-definite projection of the Gram matrix. 2. `CyclosporaClusterFinder.find_clusters(matrix, gold_or_None)` — Ward AGNES hierarchical clustering, with the number of clusters chosen either from the dendrogram merge-height gap knee (label-free, the default) or from a threshold calibrated on gold-standard labels (supervised).
-----
**Input**
- *Haplotype data sheet* — the wide CDC HDS table. Column 1 is `Seq_ID`, every other column is one haplotype name, `X` means present, an empty cell means absent. An **entirely empty locus block** means the locus was **not called**, which PyEuk treats as dropout rather than as absence; that distinction is why the sheet must be written by the `Cyclospora HDS sheet` tool rather than hand-assembled from per-specimen calls. - *Gold-standard cluster labels* (optional, off by default) — `Seq_ID` and `Cluster_alias`, with a header.
**Outputs**
- *wIBS distance matrix* — square, symmetric, zero diagonal. The header row and the first column carry `Seq_ID`s. Only the specimens that passed the completeness filter appear. - *Cluster assignments* — `Seq_ID` and `Assigned_cluster` (1-indexed). `-1` marks a specimen that the completeness filter excluded from the distance matrix; those rows are present by default so that no specimen vanishes silently, and can be suppressed under **Advanced options**.
-----
**Label-free by default, and why that matters**
The default path passes `None` where PyEuk expects a gold-standard file. No epidemiological label enters the computation, so the partition is a genuine blind prediction that can be scored afterwards. Supplying gold-standard labels switches PyEuk to calibrating its within-cluster distance threshold from those labels; the resulting clusters are then *fitted* to the labels and an accuracy computed against the same labels is not evidence of anything.
On the CDC 153-specimen reference sheet the label-free path yields k = 2 with 144 of 153 specimens passing the completeness filter, ARI 0.9721 against the Vendor_A / Vendor_B epidemiological labels.
**Version pin**
PyEuk is pinned to commit `d8e45a81` — the last commit of the **binary** KING-wIBS engine. The later SNP-weighted engine (v3.x) was benchmarked on the same sheets and regresses: AUC drops, 4 of 6 sheets collapse to k = 1, and the null controls fall from 12/12 to 10/12.
**The `epsilon` parameter is not exposed**
`PyEukDistanceEngine(epsilon=...)` parameterises the *Bayesian* distance. The revised KING-wIBS matrix computed here never reads it, so exposing it would be a knob with no effect. It is fixed at the engine default, 0.3072.
